Raw numbers copied from the console during the tests (19 Oct 2026, Linux, 4 cores shared with other helpers, Blender 5.2.2 headless, no graphics card).
The full call-by-call transcript of the texture job is in ../out/t1/t1_transcript.json (written by tests/t1_material_job.mjs).

1. Tool count (tests/t0_list_tools.mjs): 216 tools from the real MCP server; /server/handlers lists 218 routes.
   By name prefix: 65 rigging and animation, 26 materials/nodes/baking/UV, 59 modelling, 28 scene/files/import/export, 28 camera/light/world/render/compositor/vision, 10 server/helpers.
   Tool list as JSON = 151,465 characters (about 38,000 tokens at roughly 4 characters per token; rough estimate).

2. Texture job through typed tools (tests/t1_material_job.mjs): 41 calls in total (27 for the job itself, 14 deliberate probes), 1,160 ms of Blender time in total,
   each ordinary call about 16-24 ms (the add-on's work queue is polled every 16 ms), the 512 x 512 emission bake 176 ms, saving the PNG 155 ms.
   Result picture identical (largest difference 0 out of 255) to the picture made by the same job as one plain script and to the picture made by the official MCP in one call.
   Plain script on the command line, fresh Blender process each time: 1.76 s, 1.36 s, 1.27 s wall clock.
   Characters sent: typed route 2,492 characters of arguments in 27 calls and 4,520 characters of answers; plain script 16 lines, 1,193 characters.

3. Undo (exec_python enabled on a second throw-away instance, port 19878):
   Four typed calls (create u1, create u2, add node N1, add node B1) -> undo #1 removed B1, #2 removed N1, #3 removed u2, #4 refused (nothing left). One undo step per call.
   /batch with 3 successful ops then 1 failing op: the 3 successful ops stayed (not rolled back); undo #1 removed op 3, #2 removed op 2, #3 refused. One undo step per op inside a batch.
   Undo can only be reached through exec_python (no undo tool exists in the 216).

4. Call time with big scenes (30 calls each): small scene median 17.7 ms; one 164k-vertex mesh 17.8 ms; six such meshes (983k vertices) 17.9 ms.

5. One busy Blender, two callers (tests/t3b_blocking_and_ghost.py): a 2048 x 2048, 64-sample emission bake took 35.3 s (machine shared with other helpers).
   A second caller asking for "create material ghost_probe" 0.5 s after the bake started waited 30.0 s and got HTTP 504 BLENDER_TIMEOUT ("main-thread job exceeded 30.0s").
   After the bake finished the material ghost_probe existed anyway (the request that was reported as failed was carried out later).

6. Security probes on the localhost add-on (port 19877): a text/plain POST with "Origin: http://evil.example" and "Host: evil.example" was accepted and carried out (material created).
   OPTIONS requests are answered 501. No credentials were sent or asked for. /server/handlers lists the routes to anyone.
   /server/blender_quit with saveAs: answered {"quitting": true} but, in the headless mode, Blender stayed alive for 12+ s and no file was saved (the delayed action never ran).
   /server/shutdown worked.

7. Project's own test-suite (vitest, 213 tests incl. 2 skipped), run with BLENDER_PORT=19879, TMPDIR inside the sandbox: 197 passed, 14 failed, 2 skipped, 69.8 s.
   All 14 failures say "Cannot reach Blender ... fetch failed": Blender died during an EEVEE render ("Couldn't open libEGL.so.1"), taking the rest of that test file with it.
   Reproduced by hand on a throw-away instance: render_set_engine BLENDER_EEVEE + render_render_still -> empty reply, process gone.
   The same render with CYCLES worked (256 x 256, 0.8 s).
